why: Minimise a speed: a faster k never needs more hours, so 'can speed k finish in h hours?' is false then true as k grows, and the answer is the first k where it becomes true. You binary search the answer, not an array.
hints: Pick a speed and count the hours it needs. What happens to that count if you eat faster?
hours(k) = sum(ceil(p / k)) only goes down as k goes up. Binary search the smallest k with hours(k) <= h.
k lies in [1, max(piles)] (speed max(piles) needs exactly one hour per pile). Each check is O(n), so O(n log max) in total.
pitfalls: ceil(p / k) as (p + k - 1) // k; floating-point division can round wrongly for large values.
The upper bound is max(piles), not sum(piles): speeds above the largest pile change nothing.
